E01.finding: Distinct source/destination roles; destination transaction prevents init; NULL and destination error on init failure; one finish per successful init.

E02.finding: Destination API exclusion, destination shared-cache exclusion, and counter concurrency restrictions.

E03.finding: Source connection may be used otherwise; concurrent use requires configured threadsafe connections.

E04.finding: A source write transaction gives immediate BUSY. A pre-existing source read transaction is not closed by step: bCloseTrans stays false.

E05.finding: Normal inter-step writes, restart behavior, same file-backed handle exception, and repeated-restart nontermination.

E06.finding: Copied pages are updated through the source pager; an update failure can change p->rc between step calls.

E07.finding: OK versus DONE; retryable BUSY/LOCKED; fatal error handling; stored status.

E08.finding: Finish cleanup and incomplete-OK behavior; captured prose says contention does not affect finish, while release code returns current p->rc with DONE mapped to OK.

E09.finding: Destination transactions, write locking, page-size changes, and WAL/in-memory mismatch restrictions.

E10.finding: Progress reports stored prior-step values; changes can leave them stale; concurrent stepping/counter reads can be invalid.

E11.finding: Completed-copy consistency, VACUUM INTO and rsync leads, and the documentation update date.

E12.finding: An explicit source read transaction persists and sees an older snapshot; another connection may fail its COMMIT while the reader remains open.

E13.finding: sqlite3_rsync permits both origin and replica to be local; the release contains a local-to-local branch.

E14.finding: integrity_check is an appropriate structural check; foreign-key errors require a separate check. Neither candidate says integrity_check alone proves all application invariants.

E15.finding: Backup requests an exclusive write transaction, but ordinary WAL mode acquires a WAL write lock rather than the database-file EXCLUSIVE lock. Database-file exclusivity in that branch additionally depends on exclusive locking mode.

findings.detail: The claim that each step holds the source read lock only for that call needs the condition that the backup owns the source read transaction. If S already has an explicit read transaction, the code does not set bCloseTrans and leaves it open between steps. In rollback-journal operation that reader can block the active writer at commit; under a pinned read snapshot, later committed external changes are not necessarily visible to this S. Distinct handles and a prohibition on source write transactions do not exclude this legal state. X recommends a dedicated S, but does not explicitly require a fresh transaction-free S; Y allows existing-handle use. Completed-copy consistency is not refuted; the unconditional concurrency/freshness description is incomplete.

The success-path instruction says to finish, close both handles, then remove the unique staging database and sidecars after success or abandonment. The publication gate instead requires the closed staging copy to be reopened and validated before publication. Literal execution of the cleanup sequence removes a successful candidate before that gate. Reading success as already-published success does not establish the missing ordering: finish and close are themselves prerequisites of publication. A safe implementation requires resolving the text, which this review does not do. This regression is absent from the draft, where deletion was on exhaustion or fatal error.

The release-code correction about finish preserving a current BUSY/LOCKED status is valid. Calling p->rc the last stored step result is too narrow: backupUpdate can set a fatal p->rc between step calls when a same-handle copied-page update fails. Finish then returns that status rather than the last step result. The DONE-plus-finish-OK publication gate remains conservative.

The final covers stale progress and denies completion/restart-count proofs, but omits the documented condition that counters must not be read concurrently with step; the C file also warns about finish. Thread-safe source-connection use does not make these counter functions thread-safe. This is a missing legal-use condition, not a claim that ordinary serialized progress samples are wrong.

The research-stage draft says that no predecessor was supplied to that research stage and explicitly says its statuses refer to its own recommendation. The next stage has that draft as a predecessor and rejects the earlier sentence on that basis. Availability of the draft to a later stage does not contradict the earlier stage having no predecessor. The declared artifacts do not support this rejection; it is a stage-context mistake. Actual prior input delivery is not independently audited and remains outside the allowed artifact set. The final preserves the unsupported correction.

findings.severity: false exclusion rationale for an optional lead
findings.detail: The draft excludes sqlite3_rsync for local-only copying and the critique says it is only relevant with a remote target. Primary documentation explicitly permits two local paths, and the 3.51.3 implementation has that branch. The final softer wording, not indicated for this local-only destination, still carries the local-only rationale without other fit evidence. Choosing the Backup API remains reasonable; a remote requirement is not a valid capability-based reason to reject this lead. No comparative performance finding or replacement recommendation is made.

The final allows use of the existing writer source handle, but on failure instructs closing handles without distinguishing a job-owned S from an application-owned writer S. Under the unresolved same-writer-handle configuration, that cleanup can close the still-needed writer connection. This condition matters to the brief that a writer remains active. A job-owned separate source has no such ownership issue; that restriction is not made explicit.

The final repeats the captured API statement that the first step obtains an exclusive lock on the destination file, without a journal/locking-mode condition, while explicitly allowing WAL staging. The released call chain requests wrflag=2, then pagerBegin takes the WAL write lock in normal WAL mode; it acquires a database-file EXCLUSIVE lock only for exclusive locking mode in that branch. An ordinary WAL destination therefore does not support the unconditional database-file-exclusive claim. Destination API/shared-cache isolation remains required by the separate API contract; this finding does not license other destination-handle use.
